transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood CSM), Priya (Head of ML - SpectraHealth), Tom (Infra), Sarah (CTO), Aaron (SRE), Eve (PM)

Summary:
Quick mid-poc sync to review last night's TTFT/streaming runs, validate sequence-length mix, decide kernel path and fallback policy. Focus on reducing tail latencies (95/99) while keeping cost within pilot budget.

Topics:
- TTFT regressions on long prompts
- Streaming buffer/early-token policy
- Kernel selection for q4f16 quantized path vs fp16 for SpectraHealth workload
- KV cache warm-up behavior and prefix caching
- Canary/fallback model routing and rollout plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: okay everyone thanks for joining, I think we can start, um, big agenda for 30 minutes ish but we'll go 45 if needed, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Priya Anand: yep thanks Lena, quick thing, we got your runs overnight, looked promising but we're seeing a high 99th for longer sequences.
[00:20] Marco Chen: yeah that's the thing we noticed too, so to be explicit last night we ran the mixed-seq bench with a 1–8–32 distribution, and the TTFT improved at median but the 99th had a tail around 420ms on A100 fp16 under continuous batching, which is above your SLO.
[00:38] Tom Reyes: to call out, our prod distribution has more 64 and 128 tokens than the bench, I think the histogram we sent earlier was truncated, we'll attach full.
[00:50] Lena Ortiz: okay good note Tom, Priya can you confirm the percent of requests over 64 for the pilot?
[00:55] Priya Anand: rough it's 18% over 64, and about 6% over 128, so there is a meaningful tail.
[01:04] Marco Chen: that explains it — sequence length impacts KV cache reuse and kernel selection, the runtime currently picks a fused attention kernel for <=64 but falls back to a different path at >64 which increases latency, especially with streaming enabled.
[01:26] Sarah Mueller: is that a model architecture thing or runtime heuristics?
[01:29] Marco Chen: mostly runtime heuristics plus kernel availability; for some ops the optimized kernel for long sequences is less mature in the quantized path, q4f16 tends to show more variance.
[01:44] Aaron Lim: our main ask is stable 95th < 250ms, 99th < 500ms, median less critical but we want predictable billing.
[01:53] Lena Ortiz: got it. Quick reality check — we have three levers: change batching windows, enable prefix/KV caching aggressively, or route >64 to the fp16 path instead of quantized. Each has throughput/cost tradeoffs.
[02:09] Priya Anand: can you remind us cost delta if we route >64 to fp16?
[02:14] Marco Chen: ballpark for your pilot footprint it's about +22% per token cost for those requests; but tail latency drops by ~30–40% from our internal runs.
[02:26] Eve Kwan: are there opportunities for hybrid — quantized for median, fp16 for tail only?
[02:31] Marco Chen: yep that's exactly the routing idea we demoed last week — smart routing by policy: sequence-length threshold or predicted latency.
[02:40] Tom Reyes: curious about practical implementation — does that add extra cold start or double inference overhead?
[02:45] Marco Chen: minimal, it's a single routing decision at request time. The only additional cost is if we run a fast predictor then forward. For us it's cheap.
[02:53] Lena Ortiz: right, and we can do canary rollouts to measure the cost delta on 5–10% of traffic before switching full.
[03:02] Priya Anand: about streaming, we noticed early-token latency spikes when enabling 100ms chunking — any suggestions?
[03:10] Marco Chen: chunking interacts with attention windowing; if chunks are too small the runtime does more kernel invocations per token which increases per-token overhead. Increasing chunk size to 200–300ms often helps but increases perceived time-to-first-token for interactive sessions.
[03:28] Priya Anand: hmm for our use case (clinical summarization) first token within 180ms is important for UX, we can't push too high.
[03:35] Marco Chen: understood — so tradeoff: slightly larger chunk reduces 99th cost but harms TTFT for very short responses. We can explore adaptive chunking: start with small chunk then expand after X tokens.
[03:48] Sarah Mueller: is adaptive chunking supported out of box?
[03:51] Marco Chen: we've built a tiebreaker in runtime; it's experimental but we've had success internally. We'll need to validate on your seq-mix.
[03:59] Priya Anand: ok can you run a variant with adaptive chunking + prefix cache enabled?
[04:04] Marco Chen: yes, that's in my action list.
[04:07] Lena Ortiz: quick security note, SpectraHealth asked about SSO and audit logs — Jules, can you confirm we sent the SOC2 and the sample audit extract?
[04:16] Jules Park: yes sent on Friday but I'll pull the truncated log and resend, and include SSO setup steps for SAML.
[04:22] Tom Reyes: thanks, our security folks will want an audit of inference request metadata retention.
[04:27] Jules Park: will include retention policy details and KMS integration notes.
[04:31] Aaron Lim: on networking, we benchmarked peering — there's a 7–9ms variance region to region, can Redwood do keepalive or warm connections to reduce that?
[04:40] Marco Chen: we support persistent connections and keepalive; also host-based routing can prefer eu-west nodes for your region to reduce hop count.
[04:49] Priya Anand: perfect.
[04:51] Lena Ortiz: back to kernels — Marco, what kernel options should we compare in the run?
[04:56] Marco Chen: recommend comparing: A) fp16 fused attention kernel, B) q4f16 default quant path, C) q4f16 with patched long-seq kernel (the experimental one), and D) same as B but with prefix cache warm-up warmed for repeated prefixes. We'll run for n=50k tokens across the seq mix you give.
[05:16] Sarah Mueller: is the patched kernel stable?
[05:19] Marco Chen: it's experimental but has shown consistent 20–35% tail reduction in similar workloads. We'll mark it as canary only.
[05:27] Priya Anand: what about memory footprint — do we hit OOM for 128 token cases on q4f16?
[05:33] Marco Chen: q4f16 reduces memory pressure, usually safe; patched kernel has slight increase in temporary memory but within limits for A100 40GB. We'll include peak memory in the run artifact.
[05:45] Tom Reyes: please include GPU utilization and context switch metrics, we saw pauses that might correlate to multi-tenant scheduler.
[05:52] Marco Chen: yes we'll provide GPU util, kernel time breakdown, tracer logs.
[05:58] Lena Ortiz: good. Next, can we align on SLOs for the pilot? We heard 95th <250, 99th <500, TTFT <180 for short replies. Any objections?
[06:10] Priya Anand: that's acceptable as target for pilot but we'll accept a phased approach: 95th target first, then 99th within two weeks.
[06:18] Sarah Mueller: and cost alerting — if routing to fp16 pushes the pilot over budget, we need an emergency rollback.
[06:24] Lena Ortiz: yep we'll add cost guardrails and an automatic fallback policy.
[06:29] Eve Kwan: timeline?
[06:31] Lena Ortiz: Marco will run kernels and adaptive chunking bench by Friday, SpectraHealth shares full seq histogram by Thursday, then we retune and run a small canary next week.
[06:44] Marco Chen: quick technical aside — KV cache warm-up: if requests reuse prefixes we can get massive speedups; recommend instrumenting prefix reuse at your client side to annotate repeat sessions.
[06:56] Priya Anand: we do have repeated templates; we'll try to push annotations.
[07:00] Tom Reyes: also, is there support for local model pinning in Redwood Private for future on-prem? We may consider that if latency requirements tighten.
[07:09] Marco Chen: yes that's part of Redwood Private; for pilot we'll keep hosted but it's an upgrade path.
[07:15] Priya Anand: any blockers on us enabling aggressive prefix cache now?
[07:19] Marco Chen: none from infra, but need to confirm privacy settings for cached prefixes — Jules will confirm retention policy.
[07:25] Jules Park: will add that to the audit docs.
[07:29] Lena Ortiz: perfect. Any competitors or alternatives on the table from your side?
[07:33] Sarah Mueller: we're still evaluating InferScale for an on-prem option and NimbusAI for a managed path, but Redwood's latency tooling is a strong differentiator.
[07:44] Lena Ortiz: appreciated. We'll follow up with detailed run artifacts and a suggested rollout for the routing policy.
[07:50] Priya Anand: can we get a short doc that maps each tuning knob to expected delta on 95/99 and cost?
[07:58] Marco Chen: yes, we'll produce an outcomes table.
[08:02] Lena Ortiz: ok last bit — next meeting same time next week?
[08:06] Eve Kwan: works for us.
[08:08] Lena Ortiz: great, thanks everyone.
[08:10] END

Notes on transcription: minor filler words and misattributions possible, rolling timestamps approximate every ~30–60s; some technical terms may be slightly garbled (e.g., q4f16 vs q4_f16) which we will clarify in attached artifacts.
